scope: research_56_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Base64/size check uses document['size'] default bypass and unvalidated blob_sha crosses content trust boundary
findings.issue: `document.get('size',128001)>128000` means a missing size field silently passes validation instead of failing closed on unknown size, and `blob_sha` is taken from `document.get('sha')` without validating it is a 40-hex string, so unvalidated/malformed source content metadata propagates into returned evidence alongside the enforced bounds.
findings.fix: Reject documents lacking a valid integer size within the bound (treat unknown as violation), and validate blob_sha shape or omit it rather than passing arbitrary provider data through.

findings.title: Interrupted prepared step retains reserved tool_calls as consumed, overcounting budget for work that may never have occurred
findings.issue: When a cached 'read_prepared' step is rewritten to 'source_outcome_unknown', `calls += value['tool_calls']` charges the full reserved maximum as used even though the transport may never have executed (or executed partially). This is conservative for paid usage (never refund/re-read) but can starve later legitimate steps of their tool-call budget in the same run purely from an interrupted reservation.
findings.fix: Track possible-usage separately from definitely-consumed tool calls, or continue the conservative no-refund charge but document/expose it as possible rather than actual usage so budget accounting is truthful.

findings.title: window_evidence row iteration can still raise on None content despite supplied guard
findings.issue: The comprehension filter `if isinstance(row['content'],str) and row['content'].strip()` is evaluated after the expression, but Python evaluates the expression only when the condition holds for comprehension, so this specific None-content crash is actually mitigated; however `row['content'].splitlines()[0]` on a non-empty single-line string is fine, so no executable defect remains here beyond unbounded `row['content']` hashing/size with no cap on content length before hashing the full column.
findings.fix: Bound the content length used for source_version hashing (e.g. hash only up to a fixed cap) to avoid unbounded memory/CPU on oversized archive rows.

findings.summary: This round re-checks prior findings: the two prior P1s around GitHub exception swallowing (web.py:108) and non-durable read_prepared rewrite (research.py:95) are now resolved in the supplied source via explicit re-raise of CapabilityDenied/StorageError and immediate tx.put persistence of source_outcome_unknown before continuing, matching #56. The remaining items are lower-severity boundary/accounting concerns (unknown-size default bypass and unvalidated blob_sha in GitHub content handling, possible-vs-actual tool-call accounting for interrupted steps, and unbounded archive content hashing) plus unreviewed dependencies that belong in not_verified per instructions. No P0 defect found; one or more P1 boundary/accounting issues remain, so verdict is FIX_P1_FIRST.
